title: "Methods"

## Pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[hoopR box scores<br/>2002-2026] --> C[per-game efficiency]
  N[nba-data: ESPN<br/>current season + schedule] --> C
  C --> R[lagged rolling means<br/>3, 5, 10 games]
  C --> E[pre-game Elo]
  R --> G[game-level features]
  E --> G
  G --> V[rolling-origin validation<br/>2015-2025]
  G --> H[holdout 2026]
  G --> L[live 2027<br/>logged before tip-off]
```

The analysis is a [`targets`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) pipeline
with packages pinned by `renv`. `targets::tar_make()` rebuilds every table,
figure, and the paper. Current-season data comes from
[nba-data](https://github.com/kalebcoleman/nba-data), an R package that
collects, validates, and stores ESPN game data.

## Keeping the future out

- **Features use earlier games only.** A team's rolling value for game *t* is
  the mean of its games *t−w* to *t−1* in the same season. Elo ratings are
  recorded before each game's result is applied.
- **This is tested.** A test changes the result of one mid-season game and
  checks that no feature for that game, or any earlier game, changes, while
  later games do.
- **Evaluation runs forward in time.** Each validation season is predicted by
  a model trained on all earlier seasons. The classification threshold comes
  from the last validation season, not the test season. Penalties are tuned
  with folds made of whole seasons.
- **The 2025-26 test season is not used to choose between models.** The live
  2026-27 season is the only fully untouched test.

## Adding a model

Models live in `R/model_registry.R`. A model is a function that returns its
name, its feature set, and a fit function:

```r
model_random_forest <- function(games) {
  spec <- parsnip::rand_forest(trees = 500, min_n = 50) |>
    parsnip::set_engine("ranger") |>
    parsnip::set_mode("classification")
  list(
    name = "Random forest: rolling + Elo",
    features = feature_sets(games)$rolling_elo,
    fit = fit_parsnip(spec)
  )
}
```

Add `"random_forest"` to `MODEL_IDS` and run `targets::tar_make()`. Only the
new model is fitted; it appears in every table and figure, and the live job
starts logging it the next day.

## Adding a feature

Features are built in `R/features.R`. Add the new column in `build_games()`
using only earlier games (for example with `lagged_mean()`), add it to a
feature set in `feature_sets()`, and run the tests. The leakage test in
`tests/testthat/test-features.R` checks every column whose name contains
`roll`, `Elo`, or `matchup`, or ends in `_diff` or `_ratio`. Name new features
to match, or add them to that pattern.
